subject: Reserved capacity sizing: runway options and price exposure authorization
messages:
From: Emma Park <emma@astrahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, procurement@astrahealth.com
Cc:
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved capacity proposal — sizing runway questions

Jonas / team,

Thanks for the proposal deck. We reviewed the numbers with engineering and have a couple of follow-ups before we can sign up for a multi-quarter commit. High level: we like the performance profile, but have concerns about the sizing runway and how late-cycle GPU market spikes would impact our effective unit economics.

Two specific asks:
- Can you run a conservative sizing scenario for 18 months that assumes 25% higher peak token volume (we need to understand headroom)?
- What contractual protections do you offer if GPU operating costs increase (e.g., indexation, collars, or price pass-through)? We are not comfortable taking full market risk on a 12–24 month commitment without guardrails.

Attached: "AstraHealth_capacity_plan_v1.xlsx" with our baseline QPS and percentiles.

Emma Park
Head of ML Infrastructure
AstraHealth

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emma Park <emma@astrahealth.com>
Cc: procurement@astrahealth.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity proposal — sizing runway questions

Emma — thanks, this is helpful. Quick notes after a first pass (we'll follow up with a numerical scenario pack):

- We can propose three runway options:
  1) Conservative 18-month reserve = 2.5x present baseline (fastest SLA, higher cost)
  2) Phased 12-month ramp = start at 1.5x baseline → step to 2.0x at month 6 → 2.5x at month 12
  3) Elastic reserve (commit floor + burst pool) to smooth cost spikes

- Contractual protections we commonly offer: GPU-index collar (price adjusts only if observed fleet GPU cost deviates > X%), quarterly true-ups, and a capped pass-through for extreme market moves.

To move forward I need: your target percent of capacity that must be fully reserved vs. burst-tolerant, and whether you have a preferred maximum price exposure (e.g., we cap your exposure to +20% of baseline cost).

I am looping in Kimberly and Ben (pricing & sales ops) to put numbers against the scenarios and surface any approval gates. We can also schedule a 30-min ops call this week to align on QPS/latency assumptions and ramp plan.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0132

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Emma Park <emma@astrahealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-06T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity proposal — sizing runway questions

Emma / team — attaching a set of pricing scenarios (pricing_scenarios_jonas_v2.xlsx). Key points up front:

- Scenario A (12m phased ramp): effective unit price = $0.0185/token-equivalent; avg fleet exposure to GPU spot is hedged by our reserved SKUs.
- Scenario B (18m conservative reserve): unit price = $0.0168/token-equivalent (lower unit cost but higher commitment).
- Scenario C (elastic reserve + burst): blended price = $0.0198 but with a smaller upfront commit.

Price-exposure mechanics we recommend: a GPU-index collar with a band of ±15% applied to the variable component, plus quarterly true-ups. For market shocks outside ±25%, we propose a capped pass-through but that requires Finance approval. Per internal policy, any pricing change that increases discounting beyond our standard list by >30% requires VP-level sign-off.

Please confirm which scenario best matches AstraHealth's risk appetite. If you want the capped pass-through threshold lowered from 25% → 20%, we can route for expedited approval but will need a one-off exec sign-off.

Thanks — Kimberly
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing_scenarios_jonas_v2.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Reserved capacity proposal — sizing runway questions

Quick finance note for the thread:

- Approval thresholds: Sales teams can approve up to 20% additional discount on multi-year committed capacity for deals with expected ARR >= $1.2M. Anything >20% and <=30% routed to Head of Revenue; >30% requires CFO approval.
- For GPU-index collars we prefer a smoothing window (12-month rolling average) to avoid whipsaw true-ups; request to legal to translate to a quarterly true-up with a 12-month smoothing clause.
- Recommend adding a 9-month ramp milestone tied to service credits if performance or capacity delivery lags (0.5% credit per delayed milestone up to 3%).

If this becomes a 24-month contract with pass-through above 25%, escalate to exec review (we need to protect gross margins). Otherwise we can sign off operationally.

Marissa Cole
Head of Finance — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Team,

Thanks for the detail. Attached are our redlines to the SOW (SOW_AstraHealth_redlines.docx). A few clarifications:

- We can accept a phased 12-month ramp but need a contractual protection that limits our exposure to GPU cost increases to +20% (we'd prefer an absolute cap rather than a floating pass-through).
- We also want an emergency capacity swap clause in case dedicated SKUs are unavailable due to hardware shortages (CloudScale has offered marketplace overflow - included on page 7).
- Regarding service credits: can you add a clause for partial refunds if a delivery milestone misses by >14 days?

Also copying CloudScale Sales to confirm marketplace overflow terms and any pre-negotiated passthrough rates.

Regards,
AstraHealth Procurement
procurement@astrahealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: procurement@astrahealth.com, Emma Park <emma@astrahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-09T18:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AstraHealth redlines + clarification on protection mechanics

Thanks, appreciate the clear redlines. Summary and proposed authorization path so we can close quickly: 

Agreed commercial path (proposal):
- Contract: 12-month phased reserve with a 9-month ramp milestone (month 1 at 1.5x baseline; month 6 at 2.0x; month 9 at 2.5x).
- Price protection: GPU-index collar with an automatic adjustment band of ±15%; for net customer exposure between +15% and +25% we apply a capped pass-through; any exposure >+25% will trigger an expedited exec review.
- Discounting: up to 20% effective discount available under Finance operational approval (Marissa). Any request for deeper (>20% and <=30%) routed to Head of Revenue; >30% requires CFO sign-off.
- Operational: include an emergency capacity swap clause (CloudScale overflow) and a service-credit milestone for >14-day delivery misses (0.5% credit per missed milestone up to 3%).

Next steps:
1) Kimberly / Ben: finalize the numbers sheet and append the collar clause language to the SOW (I attached a DocuSign link to an initial SOW for signature; mark as "subject to redline items").
2) Marissa: please confirm operational approval for up to 20% discount for this deal (we meet the ARR threshold per preliminary forecasts).
3) Emma / Procurement: confirm you accept the collar + capped pass-through approach; if you require an absolute fixed cap (no pass-through) we may need to shift pricing or add additional term protections.

If everyone is aligned, I'll route the package for internal sign-off this week and request executive approval only if the final pricing delta goes beyond the thresholds above.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
